title: SLO-budgeted retry & hedging contract with idempotency header semantics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Different services and SDKs implement retries, backoff, hedging and idempotency headers in ad-hoc ways. That leads to unpredictable unit cost, inconsistent multi-region failover behavior, and gaps in correctness for non-idempotent operations. We need a unified contract that ties retry/backoff/hedging behavior to SLO budgets and circuit-breaker state, plus a clear idempotency header semantics for cross-region deduplication and hedged request safety.
background: Over the last 18 months we've observed multiple incidents where aggressive client retries amplified transient regional failures and caused cascading overload (see postmortems linked). Existing tickets cover retry grammar and hedging in isolation but do not define a runtime-driven policy that stops retries when SLO burn is high, nor do they standardize idempotency header names/TTL/semantic for cross-region dedupe. This ticket defines the contract and SDK surface required for a coordinated rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by Platform and SDK leads describing SLO-budgeted policy and header semantics
Specified SDK API (RetryPolicyV2) implemented in Go/TS SDKs with feature flags
Runtime accepts policy and enforces per-route SLO budgets, circuit-breaker-aware hedging limits, and returns observability telemetry
Idempotency header name and semantics documented and implemented across runtime + SDKs: header 'X-Redwood-Idempotency-V2', TTL, idempotency granularity levels
Canary rollout with two customer services showing no increase in client-visible errors and reduced p99 cost for typical workloads
Runbook updated with failure modes and mitigation steps for cross-region duplication and hedged fanout overload
tasks: Write design doc: SLO budget algorithm, hedging interplay with circuit breakers, idempotency header spec
Define RetryPolicyV2 JSON contract and proto schema for control plane
SDK changes: Go, TypeScript - add RetryPolicyV2, idempotency helper, automatic header injection
Runtime changes: per-tenant SLO budgets, hedged fanout governor, global dedupe store TTL semantics
Telemetry: add retry_count, hedged_ratio, dedupe_hits, per-request-slo-budget metrics
Integration tests: cross-region failover + hedging + idempotency dedupe
Canary plan + rollout automation with feature flags and kill-switch
decisions: Use 'X-Redwood-Idempotency-V2' as the canonical header name to avoid collisions with existing semantics
Idempotency granularity levels: 'operation' (coarse), 'request' (fine) — specified in header metadata
Hedged requests allowed only when SLO budget for the route > 25% to avoid amplifying overload
Circuit breaker OPEN state will disable hedging and reduce max retry attempts to 1
Default RetryPolicyV2 uses jittered exponential backoff with configurable hedge_window_ms and max_concurrent_hedges
Control plane exposes per-route SLO budget and hedging caps which runtime enforces dynamically
rollout_plan: Stage 1: feature-flagged SDK + runtime in staging with canary services. Stage 2: limited beta with 3 internal services (console, billing, inference-routing). Stage 3: wider opt-in for high-volume customers. Use 'slo-budgeted-retry' feature flag and a kill-switch at router level. Monitor retry amplification, p99 latency, dedupe hit rate. Rollback if hedged_ratio increases by >5% and error rate increases by >1% in canary window.
testing_plan: Unit tests for SDK helpers and header parsing. Integration tests: simulated region outage with latency spike, validate that dedupe prevents duplicate side-effects for 'operation' granularity. Load test hedged fanout under different SLO burn levels. Chaos test: flip circuit breaker states during hedged windows and assert no duplication beyond idempotency TTL.
observability_notes: Expose tokenized SLO budget in the tracing span and attach retry metadata (attempt, backoff_ms, hedged) so evaluators can tie client behavior to SLO burn. Add automatic alerts when dedupe_hits drop to zero while hedged_ratio > 0.1 indicating potential dedupe failures.
migration_notes: Backward compatible: SDK will default to legacy V1 retry behavior unless feature flag enabled. Control plane will allow 'legacy' and 'v2' policies per-customer. Provide a migration tool that scans PRs and common endpoints to mark idempotency granularity for each endpoint.
safety_and_failure_modes: If dedupe store is unavailable, runtime will fall back to synchronous single-request mode and log an error. If per-route SLO budget is not reported, default to conservative policy: retries disabled, hedging disabled. Circuit-breaker misconfiguration should not enable hedging; runtime will validate config at startup.
